original_test_intent: Verify controlled replacement rebuild of an isolated degraded RAID5, continued data access during rebuild, final parity/data integrity, and safe handling of the formerly removed member across five approved cycles.
original_method: Bind array geometry and all member/spare identities, remove one member, explicitly choose a compatible replacement, start and monitor the rebuild, perform bounded I/O, verify full rebuild/parity/data integrity, then reinsert the old member under an approved foreign/stale-metadata disposition policy.
manual_activity: Operator removes the mapped failed-test member, inserts the approved replacement if not preinstalled, and later inserts the old member only when automation confirms the controller's approved stale/foreign-member handling step.
required_inputs: Current member and replacement/spare serial/WWN-to-bay map
Vendor-approved member removal and replacement procedure
Disposable corpus and approved degraded I/O
safety_requirements: Never guess array, failed member, replacement or bay
Require optimal baseline and compatible replacement capacity
Stop on second fault, URE, wrong destination, timeout or parity error
Do not reinsert old member during rebuild
Do not import stale metadata automatically
agent_execution_scope: Inventory array geometry and all drive identities/roles
Present exact rebuild source/destination and old-member policy
Monitor degraded I/O and rebuild progress
Control old-member reinsertion as unconfigured/foreign per approved procedure
Confirm final array and all drive health
engineer_actions: Approve array, removed and replacement drives
Define rebuild direction and old-member disposition
Approve degraded I/O and five-cycle interpretation

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic enumeration and state monitoring cannot select or validate the replacement rebuild, parity result or stale old-member handling.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: For each approved cycle, capture optimal RAID5, remove the mapped member, rebuild onto the explicitly approved replacement while monitoring I/O and parity risk, validate full recovery and hashes, then insert the old member only under the documented foreign/stale-metadata policy.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: RAID5, removal, rebuild with another drive, degraded file operations, old-member reinsertion, MD5/copy checks, five repetitions and 40/20-minute timing are preserved; source/destination and final role are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a rebuild transaction ledger recording failed-test member, replacement, controller selection action, progress, I/O/error rate, parity check, corpus hashes and old-member foreign-state handling.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes rebuild direction and post-rebuild membership explicit, preventing stale member auto-import.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Detects wrong-destination rebuild, incomplete parity recovery, replacement incompatibility and hazardous reintroduction of old metadata.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Each full rebuild stresses all surviving members; repeating across all drives five times may exceed the source's 20-minute machine-time estimate and needs a project cycle interpretation.

project_override_considerations: 'Other drive' must be a named replacement/spare, and reinserting the old drive must have a documented final role. The private software-RAID script cannot define controller-specific foreign-drive policy.
expected_evidence: No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently intends a replacement rebuild followed by old-drive reinsertion. It leaves the replacement and old-member roles unspecified, but these are finite execution inputs rather than contradictory purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Rebuild source/destination, old-member policy and recovery can be supplied; execution is blocked only if they remain ambiguous or unsafe after request.

review_improvement: Prevents an unspecified rebuild target or stale former member from corrupting membership and makes full parity recovery—not mere enumeration—the acceptance evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A replacement rebuild changes array membership, unlike simply returning the removed member. Once the rebuild completes, the old member contains stale generation metadata and must be handled explicitly. Wrong rebuild direction or automatic import can destroy the recovered state, so identities, roles and parity completion require confirmation.
